shapes.production_abi: FlashInfer TRT-LLM paged FP8 sparse MLA prefill

baseline_kernel: FlashInfer TRT-LLM-gen Q64 PersistentKeepsAb sparse MLA with stock SGLang dispatch

bottleneck.evidence: Decision-bearing Nsight Compute and Nsight Systems artifacts under profile/dsa-prefill-trtllm-m4096-rawpool-tactic-oracle-20260722 show that smaller shipped query-head tactics preserve tensor work and DRAM traffic but multiply CTA waves, shared-memory instructions, bank conflicts, and synchronization without increasing occupancy. These are advisory production-ABI profiler artifacts, not frozen-task result metrics.

approaches.summary: Reached DeepseekSparseAttnBackend.forward_extend through SGLang's actual TRT-LLM-gen prefill branch with the observed raw FP8 pool, dummy page, fused physical top-k table, RoPE/quantization, KV write, and attention leaf.
approaches.why: The fixture proves the runtime class, branch, tensor ABI, and containing checkpoint-free region, but its synthetic top-k and identity correctness candidate cannot replace a live checkpoint-backed request or an independent mathematical oracle.

approaches.summary: Applied a repo-local overlay of the FlashInfer 0.6.12 selector headers and forced the shipped Q32 PersistentSwapsAb tactic only for the exact raw-pool production shape, with stock fallback on every mismatch.
approaches.why: The smaller query-head split doubled grid waves and global-load instructions, substantially increased shared-memory work and bank conflicts, and left occupancy unchanged, so every paired serving-native series regressed.

approaches.summary: Forced the shipped Q16 PersistentSwapsAb tactic through the same exact-shape source overlay to test whether finer head splitting exposed otherwise idle parallelism.
approaches.why: The finer split quadrupled grid waves and global-load instructions while increasing shared-memory and synchronization work without an occupancy benefit, producing an even larger regression.

approaches.summary: Replayed the corrected rank-local leaf independently on all four host B200s with rank-maximum timing and a single serialized profiler allocation.
approaches.why: The diagnostic established stable behavior across the available devices, but it contains no DSA collective and cannot satisfy or weaken the required TP8/DP8/EP8 production acceptance gate.

approaches.summary: Audited the earlier direct enable_pdl-disabled candidate and temporary SGLang dispatch commits against their persisted command and candidate metadata.
approaches.why: The persisted timing files measure the external leaf candidate rather than the temporary SGLang dispatch, so the neutral direct-leaf result cannot be relabeled as integrated SGLang performance.

lesson: For Blackwell sparse MLA, do not assume that splitting query heads into more CTAs improves an apparently synchronization-limited generated kernel. First compare the vendor's shipped tactic portfolio at the exact physical cache ABI: if occupancy stays fixed while waves and shared-memory synchronization multiply, retain the wider tactic and move optimization effort to a different backend seam.

caveats: This entry supersedes glm52--dsa_prefill_attn--b200--20260722a for evidence labeling: the inherited compact direct-leaf replay had 512 pages, while the reached SGLang physical ABI has 513 pages including a leading dummy page.
The earlier entry's PDL result was a direct external-candidate leaf measurement, not timing of the temporary SGLang integration; the integration was reverted and never performance-measured.
No evaluate_task.py result.json exists for this production-ABI session, so result speedups, repeat, conservative gate fields, and glm52 shape-gate counts are intentionally absent or null.

The configured GLM-5.2 checkpoint directory is empty, so live indexer output, complete model projections, scheduler behavior, and end-to-end serving were not exercised.
The host has four B200s; the unchanged eight-rank TP8/DP8/EP8 correctness and latency gate remains external and unpassed.
The checkpoint-free fixture uses deterministic synthetic physical top-k indices and process-global SGLang test seams.
No replacement was promoted; stock Q64 FlashInfer behavior remains active for every input.
